messages.subject: Recommendations for developer-only dependencies
messages.body_plain:
What's a good way to use stuff like 'devtools' and 'roxygen2' while working on an R package, while using 'packrat' to manage dependencies?

I've got 'testthat' declared in my 'DESCRIPTION' file as a "Suggests" dependency - it's only necessary for running the tests, so it makes sense to be an optional dependency.  It also makes sense to bundle the dependency in the packrat libs, on the philosophy that tests are true parts of the package, and code in the tests does call 'testthat' stuff, so we should keep track of which version we used.  So that seems all good.

On the other hand, something like 'devtools' isn't a true dependency of the package at all - it's just a helpful thing to a developer, like RStudio or a Linux box or whatever.  Yet if I don't install it in the packrat libs while doing development, I can't use stuff like 'test(filter="foo")' for spot-checking unit tests, or any of the other things it offers.

Similarly, if I'm using 'roxygen2' for managing docs & my 'NAMESPACE' file, it's not a true dependency of the package, but it's necessary for a developer, because without installing it into packrat's libs, I get "Error in loadNamespace(name) : there is no package called 'roxygen2'".

So is there a good way to have an additional set of "developer-only" dependencies, *not* to be bundled with the package when it's time to deploy?

Thanks,

 -Ken

messages.subject: Re: Recommendations for developer-only dependencies
messages.body_plain:
I had a proposed solution for this, but it doesn't work inside RStudio, only outside RStudio.

If I change my project's '.Rprofile' like so:

------------
#### -- Packrat Autoloader (version 0.4.1.24) -- ####
source("packrat/init.R")
#### -- End Packrat Autoloader -- ####
.libPaths(c(.libPaths(), "packrat/dev"))
------------

Then the extra directory gets added as expected in a command-line R session.  However, in RStudio, we hit the "escape hatch" of packrat/init.R first, then my '.libPaths(...)' line gets run, then RStudio invokes the init.R again *without* loading the .Rprofile, setting .libPaths in the process, which blows away the setting I just made.

For this particular case I can change the init.R like so:

     setHook("rstudio.sessionInit", function(...) {
-      source("packrat/init.R")
+      source(".Rprofile")
     })

but that's probably not a good fix in general because some things in people's .Rprofile wouldn't like being run twice like this.

messages.subject: Re: Recommendations for developer-only dependencies
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ken,

The recommended way to go about this is to use the Packrat 'external.packages' option. Packages set here are loaded and made available from the user library. You can use:

    packrat::opts$external.packages(c("devtools", "roxygen2"))

to make these packages available from an external library in your Packrat project.

Thanks,
Kevin

messages.subject: Managing local packages, what exactly is a "local repository"?
messages.subject_clean: Managing local packages, what exactly is a "local repository"?
messages.body_plain:
The current instructions for managing local packages built from source in both the README on CRAN and the instructions on RStudio’s github page guide the user to set the path to the local repository using packrat::set_opts(local.repos = ...) and then install using packrat::install_local().

After creating a subdirectory of my project folder to be the local repository, this has lead me to try the following:
using packrat::install_local the same way I would use install.packages, e.g.: install_local("myPackage_0.10.4.tar.gz"). After which packrat::status() complains that “No package ‘myPackage’ found in local repositories specified.”
Changing that to install_local("myPackage") which doesn’t work.
Renaming the source to “myPackage.tar.gz”, and repeating (1), giving the same error.
extracting the source package into a new sub-folder myPackage. This works, but I’m not sure if its correct?
I also briefly attempted to create a local repository following the R Administration and Installation Instructions <http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-admin.html#Setting-up-a-package-repository>, which I suspect may be the correct solution?

Some clarity in the instructions as to what exactly a “local repository” means would be helpful.
​

messages.subject: Re: Managing local packages, what exactly is a "local repository"?
messages.subject_clean: Managing local packages, what exactly is a "local repository"?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Scott,

Thanks -- you are correct that the 'local repositories' bit is unclear, and the feature is also not entirely fleshed out. What we call 'local repositories' is a separate entity from 'CRAN-like repositories'.

Perhaps we should call them 'ad-hoc local repositories', to distinguish them from 'CRAN-like local repositories', or something to that effect. But what we call 'ad-hoc local repositories' in Packrat are just directories containing package sources -- in other words, as you noted in step 4. That is the intended use of the feature.

Using a 'real' CRAN-like repository is certainly a better solution, although it would require more work to maintain. The 'local.repos' ad-hoc repository is more for very simple cases where you have a package sources that just live on disk somewhere, and just want to let Packrat know where it lives (and hence available for install).

I'll update the documentation to that effect.

Thanks,
Kevin

Kevin
